identity.defect: row locks do not serialize concurrent creates against the active cap; READ COMMITTED has no predicate locking, so two concurrent creates at two active codes both count two and commit four

findings.dispositionReason: Verified: the counted rows are never mutated by a concurrent create (the mutation is an INSERT), so EvalPlanQual recheck never applies and the newly inserted row stays invisible to the waiter's statement snapshot. The last-active-admin FOR UPDATE analogy does not transfer because there the counted rows are the mutated rows. The cap can genuinely be exceeded under concurrency.

evidence.consequence: SELECT id ... FOR UPDATE followed by count+INSERT does not prevent two waiters from both counting below the cap and inserting; acceptance criterion 活跃码上限 3 is raceable

identity.defect: create answers 201 {"join_code":{...}} but the frozen plan specifies the flat {id, code, label, created_at}

findings.dispositionReason: The plan is the decision record the issue cites and it literally freezes the flat 201 shape. The nested shape was my consistency choice, silently diverging from the written contract; unwrapping restores the planned public shape.

evidence.consequence: clients implementing the planned shape read top-level id/code and get a join_code envelope; OpenAPI and Desktop parsing codify the divergence
